chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his paternal uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: My father used to say:

Indeed, God—Mighty and Majestic—does not withdraw knowledge after having sent it down; rather, the scholar dies and takes with him what he knows, and then the crude ignorant ones succeed them, going astray and leading others astray. And there is no good in anything that has no root.

key_terms.أَصْلٌ: Root/foundation — authenticated chain back to an authoritative source
key_terms.الجُفَاة: Crude ones, the ignorant and spiritually coarse who lack proper religious grounding
key_terms.يَقْبِضُ الْعِلْمَ: Withdrawing/seizing knowledge — God does not directly remove it from the world
key_terms.يُهْبِطُهُ: He sends it down — knowledge is a divine gift that descends

ai.seo_question: How does Islam say knowledge disappears from the earth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), explaining how divine knowledge is not withdrawn from the earth by God directly, but rather disappears when scholars die. Those who succeed the scholars—being crude and ignorant—become sources of misguidance. The closing maxim warns that any teaching without a sound foundation in authenticated knowledge is without value. This teaching reflects the Imami doctrine of the indispensability of authoritative scholarly transmission and would have been understood by the audience as an argument for following the Imams as the living repositories of true knowledge.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said,

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic does not Capture the knowledge after having Sent it down, but He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes the death of a scholar, so he goes away with whatever he knew and the vanities follow them (the people), so they would be straying and causing others to be straying, and there is no goodness in something which does not originate from its source (the Divine Knowledge)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya’qub ibn Salim from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following.
“Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘My father used to say, ‘

Allah does not take back the knowledge that He has sent down. But when the scholar dies it takes away his knowledge and after this the unjust ones come and they go astray and mislead people and there is no good in things without basis.’”
